lead: Discover the secrets of Calatrava and Candela, interactive science, the planet Mars and the universe of Leonardo da Vinci with specialist guides from the CAC itself.
Four visits with specialist guides, organised directly by the City of Arts and Sciences.

items.title: Architectural visit — The architect’s eye
items.subtitle: Access to areas closed to the public · Privileged panoramic views · Two itineraries to choose from
items.body: The most exclusive visit to the City of Arts and Sciences. A route mainly through the outdoor spaces that gives access to areas normally closed to the general public, with privileged panoramic views over the whole complex. The guide uncovers the work of two magnificent architects: Santiago Calatrava — responsible for the Museu de les Ciències, the Hemisfèric, the Umbracle, the Àgora and the Palau de les Arts — and Félix Candela, the engineer who designed the Oceanogràfic with its concrete structures in the form of hyperbolic paraboloids. You can choose between two itineraries: Itinerary 1 covers the Museu de les Ciències, the Àgora, the Hemisfèric, the Umbracle and the Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía; Itinerary 2 replaces the Palau de les Arts with the Oceanogràfic.

items.title: Guided visit to the Museu de les Ciències
items.subtitle: Ideal for a first visit or groups short of time · Main exhibitions · Hands-on science
items.body: The official guided visit to the interior of the Museu de les Ciències Príncep Felip, led by specialist staff from the museum itself. It covers first-hand the contents of the museum’s most important exhibitions and shows that science can be fun and entertaining. It includes dynamic activities to discover scientific concepts in an enjoyable, participatory way. This visit is ideal for groups with little time or visiting the museum for the first time who want to get their bearings quickly across its 26,000 m² of interactive exhibition: genetics, space exploration, physics, technology and the environment. The museum opened in November 2000 and is the largest interactive science museum in Spain.

items.title: Guided visit “Mars. The conquest of a dream”
items.subtitle: The red planet · Martian craters · Similarities with Earth · History of space exploration
items.body: A specialist guided visit to the exhibition “Mars. The conquest of a dream”, one of the most visited at the Museu de les Ciències. The guide takes visitors to every corner of the red planet: its craters, volcanoes and valleys; how your voice would sound on Mars and what you would weigh there; the similarities and differences between Martian and Earth landscapes that surprise even adults. It also reviews how the perception of Mars has changed through history — from Antiquity to the first space missions — the Mars rovers and the human aspiration to set foot on the red planet. The third floor of the Museu also houses “Zero Gravity” and models of rockets, of the International Space Station and of the most famous lunar module in history.

items.title: Guided visit “Leonardo. 500 years of genius”
items.subtitle: Codices · Mirror writing · Machines · Anatomy · Immersive gallery · VR Florence flyover
items.body: A guided visit that immerses visitors in the mind and creative universe of Leonardo da Vinci to mark the museum’s 25th anniversary. The guide deciphers Leonardo’s enigmatic codices, his mirror writing, his revolutionary war and flying machines, and his anatomical studies that anticipated medical knowledge by centuries. The experience includes the immersive gallery with SENSORY4™ technology that transports visitors to the streets of Florence, the canals of Venice and the grandeur of Milan; the collection of more than 50 large-scale machines based on his sketches; interactive areas devoted to the Mona Lisa and the Vitruvian Man; and the “VR Florence flyover” virtual reality simulator. Thanks to the OrganKits project of the University of Murcia, participants also examine real organs and see how some of his anatomical theories have been confirmed in the 21st century.

blocks.title: Tips for the CAC guided visits
items: The architectural visit is the only way to access restricted areas of the complex: panoramic views and corners no ordinary visitor can see
The Science on Stage workshops (€3.50) can be bought without a Museu ticket: perfect for families short of time or to round off a partial visit
The Space Simulator also does not require a Museu ticket and is one of the most highly rated experiences for all audiences
Always confirm the programme at the ticket offices or on 96 197 46 86 before you go: guided-visit timetables and availability are subject to change
The architectural visit requires a minimum of 2 people; for the visit with tickets to the Oceanogràfic and Museu (external operators) the minimum is 4 people
Combine the guided visit to the Museu in the morning with the Hemisfèric in the afternoon: the perfect day at the CAC without crowds and making the most of your tickets
